sections.hypothesis: G1 (btc-rotation-8) earns more with a short side: while BTC closes more than 3% below its 50-day average, short the weakest 3 of its 8 coins by 90-day return. Today it sits in cash then. Hypothetical: Kestrel can't short (P5 parked; retail shorting in Australia is CFDs at 2:1, real perps are wholesale-only). A pass is recorded as needs-shorting and never traded until a licensed retail route exists.
sections.rationale: Who pays: weak coins in a falling market keep falling, as momentum losers do (the short leg of cross-sectional momentum), helped by forced selling. Outside evidence: the losers' leg of crypto momentum (Liu, Tsyvinski and Wu 2022, Journal of Finance, at 1-4 week horizons; 90 days here is G1's own lookback). Not a rejected family. Disclosed: G1's 8 coins are today's large coins (findings 15), so they are survivors: that biases this short side against itself (survivors recovered) and the long side for it. The regime margin (3% below, mirroring G1's 3% above) is fixed here, before any look. Runs: one, one trial in the main log.
sections.rules: Long side: G1 unchanged (each Sunday close while BTC closes more than 3% above its 50-day average, the top 3 of BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, DOGE, LINK, DOT, LTC by 90-day return, each 1/3 x min(1, 50% / its 30-day annualised volatility); eligible with a year of history). Short side: each Sunday close while BTC closes more than 3% below its 50-day average, short the bottom 3 by 90-day return, the same eligibility and size. Between the two, cash. Held for the week. Decide at each close, trade at the next open (the engine's convention); returns open to open, daily, 2020-01-01 to 2025-10-31 (Binance funding history starts 2020-01; nothing from the holdout). Weights in [-1, 1]: short notional never above equity, inside ASIC's 2:1 retail cap (margin 50% of notional). A short is closed out if a day's high reaches 1.5x its entry (a conservative 2:1 margin call), at that price.
sections.parameters: top_n 3, lookback_days 90, btc_days 50, margin_pct 3 (both sides), vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50. Nothing else is tried.
sections.costs: Long side as kestrel.toml (7.5 bps fee with the BNB discount plus the coin's half-spread band, on every change in weight). Short side, primary (the retail route: a 2:1 CFD like Eightcap's): 2x the coin's spot half-spread band on every change in short weight (CFD spreads are wider than spot; no commission) plus financing of 5% a year on short notional, charged daily (Eightcap's trade page lists a 5% p.a. BTC swap; whether that is the short rate is unconfirmed: check before freezing). Reported, deciding nothing (same signals, so not extra trials): the short as a Binance USDT-M perp (5 bps taker per side plus the band, and its real 8-hourly funding: a positive rate pays the short), and the CFD at 15% a year (an older Eightcap rate). Whether Eightcap offers CFDs on all 8 coins is unchecked; the perp version covers the gap (each has a Binance USDT-M perp).
